sources.title: NISAを知る（NISA特設ウェブサイト）

ruleVersions.title: Keeping NISA when leaving Japan
ruleVersions.statementEn: Account holders who leave Japan because of an employer's transfer order (or a similar unavoidable reason, including a spouse accompanying the transferee) can keep existing NISA holdings tax-exempt by filing a continuation notice (継続適用届出書) with their financial institution by the day before departure. The exemption lasts until December 31 of the year in which five years have passed since the notice. No new purchases are allowed while abroad, and a return notice (帰国届出書) must be filed within that period, or the account is closed and the holdings move to a taxable account. People leaving for other reasons must file a departure notice, and their NISA account is closed. Not every financial institution supports the continuation procedure.

value.qualifier: until Dec 31 of the year 5 years after the notice

ruleVersions.appliesTo: NISA account holders who become non-residents of Japan

ruleVersions.title: The ¥2,000 self-burden
ruleVersions.statementEn: Within the donor's deduction limit, the amount donated minus ¥2,000 is deducted from income tax and residence tax. The ¥2,000 applies once to the calendar year's total donations, not to each donation.
ruleVersions.appliesTo: Furusato nozei donors within their deduction limit

ruleVersions.title: One-stop exception conditions
ruleVersions.statementEn: Salaried people who do not otherwise need to file a tax return can use the one-stop exception if they donate to five or fewer municipalities in a year (repeat donations to the same municipality count once toward the five). Applications must reach each municipality by January 10 of the following year. Filing a tax return voids all one-stop applications, so every donation must then be declared on the return.
ruleVersions.appliesTo: Salaried furusato nozei donors who do not file a tax return
